'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**Two [[missile]]s are launched against a [[mosque]] in [[Marib Governorate]], killing and injuring a total of 29 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/1/houthi-missile-attack-on-mosque-kills-29-says-yemen-minister (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Gunmen [[mass shooting|open fire]] against security forces in [[Sourou Province|Sourou]], [[Burkina Faso]], killing five policemen. Fifteen attackers are killed in a gunfight after the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/armed-group-kills-five-policemen-northern-burkina-faso-2021-10-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Salisbury rail crash]]
**Seventeen people are injured in a [[derailment]] and [[train wreck|crash]] between two trains near [[Salisbury]], [[Wiltshire]], [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-59114569 (BBC News)]
*One person is killed and 15 others are injured when a [[Pemex]] [[gas pipeline]] explodes in [[Puebla]], [[Mexico]]. The [[Governor of Puebla]], [[Miguel Barbosa Huerta]], blames an illegal tap for the explosion. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7491689/pemex-pipeline-blast-in-mexico-kills-one/ (''The Canberra Times'')]
*Nine [[firefighter]]s are killed during a training exercise inside a cave in [[Altinópolis]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]], [[Brazil]], after the roof of the cave collapsed. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/nine-brazil-firefighters-die-after-cave-collapse-during-training-exercise (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****[[Myanmar]] surpasses 500,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/asia/covid-19-cases-surpass-500000-in-myanmar20211031204136 (Asian News International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] issues an emergency use authorization of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] for children aged 5 to 11. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/uae-approves-pfizer-covid-19-vaccine-ages-5-11-2021-11-01/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 40,993 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 8.51 million. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/russia-hits-high-daily-coronavirus-cases-80885720 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] says that she has tested positive for COVID-19 following a meeting with [[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]]. She said in a statement that she is experiencing mild symptoms. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jen-psaki-covid-19-tests-positive/ (CBS News)]

'''International relations'''
* [[India]]n Prime Minister [[Narendra Modi]] visits [[Pope Francis]] in the [[Vatican City|Vatican]]. It is the first-ever meeting between the two leaders. Modi is in Rome for the [[2021 G20 Rome summit|G20 Heads of State and Government Summit]], October 30-31, before he flies to [[Glasgow]], Scotland, for the 26th United Nations Conference on Climate Change ([[2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP26]]), October 31 to November 12. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2021-10/pope-francis-india-prime-minister-modi-meeting.html (Vatican News)] [http://asianews.it/news-en/Pope-receives-Narendra-Modi-who-invited-him-to-visit-India-54400.html (Asia News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[October 2021 Tokyo attack]]
**A man attacks passengers on a train in [[Chōfu]], [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]], with acid and a knife, before [[arson|setting the train on fire]], injuring 17 people. A man is arrested at the scene. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/knife-arson-acid-attack-tokyo-train-leaves-about-10-injured-media-2021-10-31/ (Reuters)]
*The [[National Guard (Mexico)|Mexican National Guard]] open fire against a vehicle carrying [[Cuba]]n citizens, killing one person and wounding four more people. The guards said that "the vehicle didn't stopped when ordered to do so". [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexicos-national-guard-kills-cuban-migrant-wounds-four-others-caravan-advances-2021-11-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Japanese general election]]
**[[Japanese people|Japanese]] citizens head to the polls to elect members of the Lower House. The ruling [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]] faces more opposition than in previous elections due to the handling of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|COVID-19 pandemic in the country]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/japan-election-ldp-parliament/2021/10/31/9acfc4c8-38aa-11ec-9662-399cfa75efee_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[October 2021 Sudanese coup d'état]]
**[[Prime Minister of Sudan|Sudanese Prime Minister]] [[Abdalla Hamdok]] says that he will not step down despite being under [[house arrest]] following the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|military]] [[coup]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/10/31/africa/sudan-prime-minister-hamdok-military-coup-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Prime Minister of North Macedonia|North Macedonian Prime Minister]] [[Zoran Zaev]] announces his resignation following a decisive defeat of his party, the [[Social Democratic Union of Macedonia|Social Democratic Union]], in the local elections. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-elections-local-elections-northmacedonia-skopje-1edf324bbcc88a4239d625e2884fc794 (AP)]
